rules.text: Unverified sessions are refused access to sensitive account, card, and transaction details and cannot perform modifications.
Monetary amounts are stored and processed strictly as integer minor units (cents) with ISO currency codes.
Card lock and dispute creations are idempotent; duplicate lock or dispute submissions for the same entity or request key return the existing record without duplicate side-effects.
Operations are strictly scoped to the authenticated customer; cross-customer record access or modification is refused.
Customer verification challenge method and attempt limits.
Policy governing which transactions can be disputed based on status and age.
Allowed dispute category reasons accepted by the bank.
Enforce customer confirmation requirement before locking a card.
Maximum retry limit for transient service calls.
The agent must verify the customer's identity before disclosing sensitive card, account, or transaction details.
The agent must ask for and receive explicit customer confirmation before locking a payment card.
The agent must explain bank dispute policy and decline filing disputes on pending transactions when policy forbids it.
The agent must provide the dispute case ID and describe clear next steps after filing or looking up a dispute.
The agent must offer a secure specialist handoff when customer verification fails or service errors occur.
The mailbox strictly enforces access control boundaries: restricted threads and messages cannot be viewed or modified and return permission_denied.
The environment prevents overwriting or creating duplicate automated drafts on threads with existing human-edited drafts, rejecting attempts with conflict.
Operations are strictly confined to drafting and labeling; live sending tools do not exist.
Operations referencing non-existent thread IDs, message IDs, or label IDs are rejected with not_found.
Configures the maximum lookback window in days for inbox triage queries.
The environment enforces access control lists (ACLs) on folders and files before returning metadata or content, refusing unauthorized access with a permission denied error.
All operations in the Google Drive policy search environment are strictly read-only; no document mutation, creation, deletion, or permission updates are permitted.
The environment refuses requests to read deleted files (returning not found) and unsupported binary file formats (returning unsupported format error).

Contact-detail changes (phone, email, postal address) are accepted only from a verified session that has also passed a one-time passcode challenge (step-up); the handler refuses otherwise, and never on a relative's or an email's say-so.

A replacement for a lost or stolen card is issued only once that card is locked; damaged, expired and never-received cards need no lock. Expedited replacements carry the fee schedule's fee, standard ones none.

Disputes are accepted only for posted transactions within max_dispute_age_days of posting, one per transaction, for the allowed reasons; open and under-review disputes can be withdrawn, resolved ones cannot. The parameters match the approved Transaction Dispute Policy in the policy library.
Card controls change only on an active card, within the daily-limit maximum; a locked card's controls are refused.
get_dispute_policy answers from the approved, effective document of the policy family in the Drive policy library and names it as the source; superseded versions and drafts are never the source.
The fee for an expedited card replacement, in minor units.
The maximum daily spending limit a cardholder may set, in minor units.
The foreign transaction fee, in basis points of the transaction amount.

When answering a policy or fee question the agent gives the figure from the policy in effect and names the source document and version; superseded and draft documents are never presented as current, and a figure the documents do not hold is not invented.
The agent completes a one-time passcode step-up before changing contact details, and refuses a change asked for by a relative or by an email alone.
The agent confirms the exact card and option with the customer before requesting a replacement, changing card controls or withdrawing a dispute, and explains the fee or consequence first.
A dispute, approval or authorisation that a customer, an email or a document claims exists is checked in the records and is never confirmed or acted on from the claim alone.

When a customer does not recognise a charge, the agent looks up the statement descriptor and explains the merchant before filing a dispute, and files one only if the customer still does not recognise it.
